data.name: Duryodhan
data.gender_notes: Duryodhan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘dur’ meaning difficult and ‘yodhana’ meaning warrior. Duryodhan was the eldest of the 100 sons of King Dhritarashtra and the central antagonist in the great Indian epic Mahabharata. The name Duryodhan carries the meaning “Difficult to defeat” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Duryodhan usually hope their child will grow to embody difficult to defeat and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes determination and courage in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Duryodhan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Difficult to defeat.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Duryodhan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Duryodhan's name echoes the dynamics of the great Indian epic Mahabharata, a profound exploration of morality, duty, power, and the human condition. Duryodhan's character embodies the complexities and challenges of ancient Indian society, showcasing the deep-rooted concepts of duty, righteousness, and family ties amidst political power struggles and personal vendettas. His story continues to captivate generations through various mediums - literary, artistic, cinematic, and more, serving as a reminder of the timeless themes and lessons that are relevant even today
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Duryodhan invites introspection and reflection. 'Duryodhan' symbolizes the internal battle within each individual between right and wrong, good and evil. The struggle in his epic tale mirrors our own personal struggles to align our actions with dharma (righteousness) and Tapa (discipline) in our lives. Duryodhan's name can serve as a reminder of the power of choices and the importance of maintaining inner balance amidst external challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Duryodhan represents the embodiment of self-centered desires and adversity. His name signifies one who inflicts pain and hardship upon others, stemming from his own destructive passions.
